About the Project

The Applications of Quantum Technologies CDT offers a funded doctoral training route in quantum research. Recruitment for the next intake is expected to begin in November 2026. Applicants should use the new project list and partner-university guidance once the call opens.

Research Areas

  • Quantum technologies
  • Physics
  • Engineering

Funding and Duration

ComponentDetails
Award or positionPhD scholarship / studentship
Stipend / salaryFour-year stipend and tuition; amount not stated
DurationFour years

Eligibility and Requirements

Applicants are expected to meet the CDT’s academic requirements for doctoral training in quantum technologies. Candidates whose first language is not English must demonstrate proficiency through IELTS or an accepted equivalent, and visa requirements are published on the programme site.

Application dates

ComponentDetails
Recruitment statusUpcoming: applications expected November 2026
Deadline / consideration roundClosing date not yet announced
LocationUnited Kingdom

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Official Link

Full announcement and application portal: https://www.aqt.ac.uk/how-to-apply/

Source: aqt.ac.uk - the details in this listing were recorded from this official page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: Closing date not yet announced - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  1. Review the official programme page and check the opening date for the next call.
  2. Use the new call to select a project or research area and identify the documents required for that application route.
  3. Complete the submission when the application window opens, using the new deadline rather than an earlier recruitment cycle.

About University of Strathclyde

The University of Strathclyde is a partner in the Applications of Quantum Technologies doctoral training programme. The CDT brings together quantum research and training across its partner universities; applicants follow the guidance for their selected research project and host.

Official details: Read the programme or project information

Application route: Follow the official application instructions
